assessment.concept: Modern Greek language, literature and source-based cultural study
assessment.assessment: Literary studies, stylistics, psycholinguistics and creative practice support methods of language and textual inquiry. Greek myth and tragedy appear within comparative literature. The trial does not support sustained Modern Greek acquisition, Greek literature, translation or analysis of modern Greek texts.

assessment.concept: Modern Greek history, society and identity
assessment.assessment: The trial provides comparative imperial and modern history, social theory, cultural memory methods and Greek antiquity. Renaissance Mediterranean art supplies historical exchange perspectives. It does not sustain the study of modern Greece and Cyprus or the transition from Byzantine and Ottoman societies to modern Greek cultural life.

assessment.concept: Greece in Europe, the eastern Mediterranean and contemporary politics
assessment.assessment: EU law and politics, international relations, conflict, public policy and economic analysis provide relevant comparative frameworks. The trial does not develop sustained Greek-European relations, Greek or Cypriot institutions, regional political history or inquiry into Greek journalistic sources.

academicConstruction: Built three 24-course trials. Literary and language inquiry combines psycholinguistics, all six literature courses, rhetorical and creative work, Greek antiquity, art and media analysis and historical methods. The second trial tests cultural memory and identity through comparative history and sociology, heritage, museums, Greek antiquity and documentary. The third tests European and regional politics through EU law and politics, international relations, peace and conflict, comparative institutions, public economics and historical inquiry. All have at least six level-3 courses and pass current feasibility. The Greek-archaeology description and Renaissance Mediterranean art description are substantive evidence. Their relevant contributions do not establish Modern Greek specialisation. GOSHIST312 is assessed from the current official description and title, without the excluded historical outline. Empires and modern history provide comparative contexts, but a sequence in modern Greece, Cyprus, Byzantine-to-modern continuity and their literatures is absent. All 151 active identities and the content of plausible language, literary, regional, political, historical and methodological courses were screened.
distinctness: Three different disciplinary trial emphases were tested. None meets programme-level comparability and none is selected.
